measurement: Quiet history pruning, the history skip (tier 2, T24; the engine survey's B13; owner, 2026-11-11: 'Build quiet history pruning (B13) with a threshold chosen to actually fire (quick measurement first), then design R at STC'). At a non-PV node out of check, at most HistorySkipMaxDepth deep, once a move has been searched and past late move pruning, a quiet move whose ordering score (quiet_order_score) is at or below -HistorySkipPerPly x depth is skipped. This file declares the rule that picks the candidate values of HistorySkipPerPly, before the measurement's run; the head-to-head (tools/github/h2h_run.sh) then chooses among them, and design R decides adoption.
declared: 2026-11-11, before the game replay's run (revision 2; revision 1 is in 'history')
history: Revision 1 (2026-11-11, before its run) measured on the bench (46 positions to depth 13, history cleared per position) with bins of 500: 4,947,730 sites at depths 1-3 (d1 3,002,379, d2 1,222,017, d3 723,334), 44.2% of them with a negative score but almost all within (-500, 0): P = 500 skips 7.0%, 1000 1.9%, 2000 0.16%, 3000 0.01%, so no grid value of 500 came near 10% or 20%. The bench clears history per position, while a game carries it from move to move (tests/test_search_stats.cpp: the carried history has larger values), so revision 2 measures on replayed games with history carried, in bins of 100.
engine: tier2/qhp with the switch off (r8brft1, phase-4 4470f24's search), clang-stats build (FORK_SEARCH_STATS: history_skip_site_bins, the ordering score of every quiet move at a site where the skip could act, by remaining depth, in sign-magnitude bins of 100)
positions: tools/measure/game_replay.py: 48 games picked by its seeded shuffle (seed 20261111) from the r8b-rft-stc SPRT's stage 0 PGNs (8+0.08; the 'test' side is r8brft1, the current default net), every position where 'test' was to move, replayed as a game (one process per game, ucinewgame once, history and TT carried), go nodes 200000 (about an STC search's size), Hash 16 MB, no tables
max_depth_reason: HistorySkipMaxDepth stays at Fork's earlier placeholder, 3 (tier2/b4 d2b086d), below LmpMaxDepth 4; only the per-ply threshold is chosen here
grid: HistorySkipPerPly in multiples of 100 from 100 to 12000: every threshold -P x d (d = 1-3) is then a bin edge, so each predicted share is exact (the test is 'at or below'); P = 0 is left out, since it would skip every quiet move without history (score 0)
rule: For each target share t of eligible quiet moves (sites at depths 1-3), the candidate is the grid value P whose predicted skip share (sites with score <= -P x depth over all sites at depths 1-3, with the switch off) is nearest to t; a tie goes to the larger P (the more cautious). A target no grid value comes within half its own size of (|share - t| > t / 2) is dropped and the report says so; two targets landing on the same P give one candidate. Each candidate is then built with the switch on, and its actual skip share (history_skips over the sites at depths 1-3 of the same replay with the switch on) and its bench node change are recorded. The head-to-head's preferred value is the largest candidate P (the fewest skips: the most cautious).

results.run: 2026-11-11, 3:27-3:36 PM EST (switch off) and 3:38-4:04 PM EST (candidates); clang-stats builds of tier2/qhp's tree; tools/tier2_measure/history_skip_rates.py
results.notes: With the switch on the skip fires about three times as often as predicted from the switch-off distribution, presumably because skipped moves feed back into the histories (UNVERIFIED; at depth 1 the share of sites at or below -5000 rises from 0.7% off to 7.1% at 2300); the replays' site counts grow. The skip count equals the histogram's count at or below each threshold exactly (2300: 54,916,313 both), as tests/test_search_stats.cpp checks. The earlier placeholder 2500 predicts 4.1% in games against 0.04% on the bench: the bench clears history per position, which is why the tier2/b4 variant hardly changed the bench. The candidates' replays ran with game_replay.py --no-bench-check (their bench differs from the reference by design); each candidate's bench is given above.
